basis: Defining hypogonadotropin deficiency and retinal degeneration; osteoporosis 80-99% and dental abnormalities 30-79% support bone and dental involvement.
Lysosomal oligosaccharide storage disorder; intellectual disability 80-99% and ataxia 30-79%. Hearing, skeletal, ocular and immune deficits are each below 30% in this adult form.
ACTA2-related thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection; other vascular manifestations share the cardiovascular axis. No common direct damage to another axis established.
Umbrella for congenital structural heart defects; no additional organ involvement shared across most subtypes.
Riboflavin transport disorder with motor and cranial neuropathy; sensorineural deafness is a defining syndrome feature despite 2/9 in the supplied series. Stridor alone adds no organ.
Disorder located in the thalamus; visual and movement abnormalities arise from central nervous system dysfunction.
Echinostoma flukes infect the intestine. The ocular child subtype does not establish ocular involvement across this umbrella.
GNAT1-related retinal rod phototransduction dysfunction causes congenital stationary night blindness; no separate neurologic involvement.
Dermatophyte fungal infection directly involves the deep dermis.
Persistent movement disorder reflecting dysfunction of central motor circuits; abnormal movements do not establish primary muscle damage.
Bacterial infection; wound destruction and septic bullous or necrotic skin lesions together affect over 30% across typical clinical presentations. Gastroenteritis is a minority form.
Premature fusion of both coronal sutures and the sagittal suture is a structural skull disorder; neurologic damage is not established as common.
Defining severe lung disease and T-cell deficiency; cerebral abnormalities with developmental delay support CNS involvement (calcification 2/2); eczematoid dermatitis 2/4. Small series.
Mitochondrial ATP synthase deficiency; developmental delay, refractory seizures, dystonia and brain atrophy occur in the sole reported patient (1/1).
Lysosomal storage with defining neurodevelopmental disease; muscle hypoplasia 80-99%, skeletal dysplasia/bone loss 30-79%, skin ulcers 30-79%. Renal and hepatic findings below 30%.
Inherited syndromic cerebellar dysfunction; hepatic, metabolic and vestibular manifestations vary by subtype and do not apply across most of the umbrella.
Poliovirus directly destroys central motor neurons, causing paralysis; weakness and denervation do not establish an independent primary muscle disease.
Inherited glomerular disease causing nephrotic syndrome and renal failure; direct ocular dysfunction is common: reduced acuity 8/8, retinal detachment 5/9 and retinopathy 3/9.
Neoplasm originates in the sigmoid colon; no additional commonly damaged organ is established.
Basaloid squamous cell carcinoma arising in the skin.
Disorder of respiratory airflow, encompassing central and obstructive apnea; neurologic injury is not shared across the group. Cyanosis and bradycardia are signs.
Acute gonococcal bacterial infection of the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis.
Degeneration and diminished size of the thyroid gland; an autoimmune cause is not specified.
Transmissible prion disease directly causes spongiform brain degeneration; visual and motor manifestations do not establish common independent eye or muscle damage.
Defined by developmental delay or intellectual disability. Hypotonia and variable overgrowth do not establish direct muscle or endocrine disease.
